newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weak stocks don't mean Japan economy dire -- bosses.
newsitem.headline: Weak stocks don't mean Japan economy dire -- bosses.

text.p: The sharp decline in stock prices in recent sessions does not necessarily mean that the Japanese economy is in dire straits, Jiro Nemoto, chairman of the federation of employers' associations (Nikkeiren), said on Monday.
Nemoto told a regular news conference that business conditions vary in different sectors.
Asked about recent falls in stock prices, Nemoto said: "It does not mean that danger signals are flashing about the Japanese economy."
But he also warned that stocks could fall again if legislators failed to tackle issues concerning the budget and structural reforms in a parliamentary session later this month.

The stock market has been spiralling downwards on worries about a possible downturn in the economy and about the health of the banking sector, which is burdened by bad debts. A lack of confidence in government economic policy has speeded the descent.
But stock prices rebounded on Monday, with the key Nikkei average of 225 leading shares soaring 815.14 points to end at 18,118.79. The Nikkei fell more than 2,000 points last week.
